title: Arthur Schutt and the Georgians' effect on Chicagoans
summary: Ashcraft says Schutt influenced them most after Hines, perhaps via the Georgians heard in New York.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: You'll have to pick just the right day and early in it. The Artie shot, I would say probably had more effect on all of us than anybody else, short of Hines. And I guess, I can't figure out what records necessarily those were unless they were the Georgians. And I'm not sure that the Georgians were that well known.

No, but of course the Red Nickels. Yeah, he was on some of them. When 28 began to introduce Shutt, but you think that the influence was felt earlier than that. You had heard Shutt in New York as early as 25 or 26, hadn't you?
That was with a small group of Alamec, you said.
Yes, it was what had been a small unit of the Speck band. And whether the whole Speck band was still playing or not, I don't know. I don't imagine they were.
